To: Renters Board / Notices
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: URGENT: stop using Brightline Pro 6% developer, batch LX2291

Please check your Brightline developer today, including anything already open in your trolley. A client here has ended up with a painful, burnt scalp, so this is a safety issue, not just the “inconvenience” described in the supplier’s email.

WHAT’S AFFECTED

Kelvin Trade says a filling error affects Brightline Pro 6% (20 vol) Cream Developer 1L, batch LX2291. Bottles from this batch may actually contain 12% (40 vol) developer.

These bottles were supplied between 19 October and 5 November 2026. According to Kelvin Trade, other batches and other strengths are not affected.

We’ve already had two worrying experiences here. In one, a bleach retouch lifted to near pale yellow in about 18 minutes instead of the usual 35–40, and the client was left with a red, sore scalp. In another, highlights lifted very quickly, the foils became roasting hot and the result was brassy and patchy.

Double-strength developer can lift and process much faster than expected, over-process or damage the hair, and cause excessive heat, scalp burns and poor colour results. Don’t assume it’s fine because your usual mix and timing have always worked before.

HOW TO CHECK YOURS

Look at the base of the bottle for the batch code. The box does not show it, so checking the box or shelf label isn’t enough.

Check:
• Part-used and newly opened bottles in your trolley or at your station.
• Unopened stock in the back, cupboards or anywhere else you keep colour.
• Every bottle individually, even if others bought at the same time were a different batch.

If the base says LX2291, STOP USING IT immediately. Put it somewhere separate and clearly mark it DO NOT USE. Don’t pour it away or put it back into general stock.

RETURNS – BUT KEEP ANY INCIDENT BOTTLE

Unused or opened bottles with no problem attached can go back to the Kelvin Trade rep when he’s in on Tuesday, or to the Hillington depot, for full credit.

If you’ve had a reaction, unusual heat, unexpectedly fast lift or another problem, KEEP THAT BOTTLE BACK. Don’t bin it and don’t hand it back with the rest. Keep the batch marking visible, take dated photographs, keep your notes and record what products and timings you used. If there’s been an injury, speak to your own insurer as well.

IF SOMEBODY REACTS IN THE CHAIR

Stop the service straight away. Remove foils/product and rinse with plenty of cool or lukewarm running water. No shampoo.

For a suspected chemical burn, protect yourself with gloves, carefully remove contaminated clothing if possible, and continue rinsing for about one hour. Don’t apply creams or other chemicals.

Call 999 for medical help immediately for a suspected chemical burn. Don’t wait for blistering or severe pain. Chemical burns need hospital assessment. Breathing difficulty, throat swelling or collapse also need an immediate 999 call. Follow the call handler’s instructions.

Write it in the incident book at the desk and keep dated notes and photographs.

Please check yours before your next colour service.

Kirsty
